title: Order totals that refuse to overflow

blocks.text: `int` arithmetic wraps silently: `Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1` is `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, and a price times a quantity can come out small or negative, which an attacker can use to pay less. The page's fix is `Math.addExact` and `Math.multiplyExact`, which **throw `ArithmeticException`** instead. Its edge cases add a trap: `-Integer.MIN_VALUE` and `Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE)` are both still `Integer.MIN_VALUE`.
Write `OrderMath` with three methods that throw `ArithmeticException` on any overflow:

items: `total(lines...)`: the sum of the line totals, **checking every addition**.

cases.says: A line of 3 items at 1999 cents is 5997, the lines 5997 and 1000 total 6997, and the distance between 3 and 10 is 7.
A price times quantity above Integer.MAX_VALUE throws ArithmeticException instead of wrapping to a small or negative total.
Adding lines whose sum passes Integer.MAX_VALUE throws ArithmeticException, even when a later line would bring it back into range.
distance(Integer.MIN_VALUE, 0) throws ArithmeticException, because Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) is still negative.

concepts: Math.addExact and Math.multiplyExact throw ArithmeticException instead of silently wrapping, and Integer.MIN_VALUE survives negation and abs unchanged.
